rem:torus-knot-zero-volume-via-reeb:
Remark Torus-knot trajectories have zero hyperbolic volume via Reeb. The 3-cycle braid words \sigma_1\sigma_2 and \sigma_2\sigma_1 rotate all three colour tubes uniformly with rate \dot\psi = \pm q. The trajectory traces a helix on a Heegaard torus T^2 \subset S^3. The trajectory completes a T_{2,3} torus knot (trefoil).

The complement of any torus knot admits a Seifert fibration. It supports no hyperbolic structure, meaning V_{\mathrm{hyp}}(T_{m,n}) = 0. The global-vortex flow maintains parallel strands, aligns with the Hopf fibre, and closes onto the Heegaard torus, guaranteeing a Seifert-fibered complement.

Consequently, the topological mass component of the Markov-trace observable vanishes for torus configurations. Torus knots yield zero hyperbolic volume, contributing only to the counting part of the trace.

The vanishing is corroborated at the level of quantum-invariant asymptotics. The colored Jones polynomials of a torus knot admit no volume-type limit: at the Kashaev point the growth is polynomial rather than exponential, and the deformed limit J_N(T_{m,n}; e^{2\pi i r/N}) degenerates to the inverse Alexander polynomial 1/\Delta(T_{m,n}; e^{2\pi i r}) for \mathrm{Im}\, r < 0 while producing a pure Chern–Simons phase for \mathrm{Im}\, r > 0, discontinuously across the real axis [murakami2004a]. No continuous volume-like potential exists for a torus knot; any mass carried by a torus-knot particle must therefore enter through a different chain than the volume route.
rem:hyperbolic-knot-positive-volume-via-:
Remark Garside / Borromean trajectories have positive hyperbolic volume via Reeb. The Garside element \Delta_3 and the Borromean braid (\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^3 form non-torus Reeb-flow trajectories with positive hyperbolic volume.

The Garside flow swaps the red and blue tubes across three sub-intervals. It crosses between the two Heegaard tori. Its complement is not Seifert-fibered, and its JSJ decomposition contains a hyperbolic piece with a strictly positive Bloch–Wigner sum.

The Borromean braid traces a link whose complement is the Gieseking–Meyerhoff manifold. Its hyperbolic volume is V_{\mathrm{hyp}} = 8\,G, derived from two regular ideal octahedra.

The figure-eight knot 4_1 sits between the trefoil and the Borromean link. Its complement has hyperbolic volume 2 v_3 \approx 2.0299, the least volume of any orientable cusped hyperbolic 3-manifold (a minimum it shares with its sister manifold) [hodgson2012], and the unique minimum among hyperbolic link complements in S^3 [kegel2024]. Its Reeb-flow trajectory \sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1}\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1} crosses between Heegaard tori twice.

Only hyperbolic pieces contribute to the JSJ-graded mass factorization. Torus trajectories remain geometrically invisible because they never enter the bulk hyperbolic regime. The trajectory pattern determines the JSJ verdict.
rem:hyperbolic-volume-degeneracy-prior-a:
Remark Prior art: hyperbolic volume does not determine the manifold. By Jørgensen and Thurston, only finitely many orientable hyperbolic 3-manifolds have a given volume v; write N(v) for that number. Hodgson and Masai record that it is often larger than one [hodgson2012, \S 1, pp. 1--2]. At the lowest cusped volume v_\omega = 2.029883\ldots there are exactly two cusped manifolds, the figure-eight knot complement and its sister m003 (Cao–Meyerhoff). For link complements in S^3 the count grows at least exponentially: for each n \ge 3 there are at least 2^n/(2n) hyperbolic link complements of volume 4nV_8, where V_8 is the volume of the regular ideal octahedron [hodgson2012, Thm 8.5, p. 22].

For the volume of the Reeb-bundle complement this sets a scope: \mathrm{Vol}(K) is a well-defined invariant of each knot or link, but it is not an identifying label. Two different link complements can have the same volume, so a quantity that depends on K only through \mathrm{Vol}(K) cannot tell them apart. In particular \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) is also the volume of the sister manifold m003. The paper says nothing about the other factors of the mass law, so it neither supports nor rules out any QOU mass assignment.

conj:hecke-monodromy-step-two:
Conjecture The Hecke quadratic is the q-deformed branch-point monodromy of the colour cubic (Step 2 of the canonical chain as a conjecture). Let P(X, z) = X^3 + (z+1)X^2 + (z^2+z+1)X + (z^3+z^2+z+1) be the colour cubic, whose root X(z) and its jets are the Seiberg--Witten periods, and let \Delta \subset \mathbb{C} be its discriminant locus in z. The substrate connection on \mathbb{C} \setminus \Delta has braid-group monodromy \varrho \colon B_n \to H_n(q) into the Hecke tower carrying the Markov trace, such that for every generator g_i = \varrho(\sigma_i):

  1. the Hecke quadratic g_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\, g_i + 1 holds, together with the braid relation g_i g_{i+1} g_i = g_{i+1} g_i g_{i+1} and far commutation;
  2. the tower is defined over the Laurent ring \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}], and the classical specialisation \varepsilon \colon H_n(q) \to \mathbb{Q}S_n sends q \mapsto 1; then each g_i becomes an involution, \varepsilon(g_i)^2 = 1 --- the Picard--Lefschetz transposition of the two roots of P that collide at a branch point.

The two eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} of the monodromy quadratic F(\sigma) = \sigma^2 - (q - q^{-1})\sigma - 1 are then a consequence: (g_i - q)(g_i + q^{-1}) = 0. The polynomial F is an eigenvalue relation of the monodromy of a flat connection, not a curvature: a curved connection has path-dependent holonomy and gives no braid representation. For the \mathfrak{sl}_2 Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov connection on two points, the quadratic and the involutive shadow are theorems, derived from the Casimir eigenvalues \tfrac12 and -\tfrac32.
rem:vertex-operator-dictionary:
Remark VOA--QOU dictionary. The vertex operator definition establishes the dictionary between the standard VOA formalism and QOU structures. The classical connection relies on the KZ equation for the WZW model, where monodromy corresponds to the R-matrix of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)). The QOU makes this correspondence geometric.

The CFT worldsheet is the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}). The target space is the Reeb bundle \mathcal{R}_p \to \mathcal{S}_p. The time direction is the Reeb flow \xi_q. The state space at fixed time is the brane tower \bigoplus A_n. The Reeb bundle serves as the arena for braiding and as the total space of the string whose quantisation yields the VOA. The substrate parameter q = e^{2\pi i/(k+2)} links algebraic deformation to the geometric pitch of the Reeb connection; at the real substrate pin q_0 \approx 1.11 this forces a non-unitary level, k + 2 = 2\pi i/\ln q_0 \approx 60.218\, i (Hecke monodromy conjecture).

thm:centre-cocentre-descent:
Theorem Centre–cocentre splitting: A = Z(A)\oplus[A,A] gives a unique descended/transient split that every trace sees only through its central part. Let K be a commutative ring and A a K-algebra. Write Z(A) for its centre and [A,A] for the K-span of all commutators ab-ba. Suppose A = Z(A)\oplus[A,A] as K-modules (a centre–cocentre splitting), and let \pi_Z : A\to A be the projection onto Z(A) along [A,A]. Put x^{\mathrm{desc}} := \pi_Z(x), x^{\mathrm{trans}} := x-\pi_Z(x) and \theta_Z := 2\pi_Z-\mathrm{id}_A. Then:

  1. x = x^{\mathrm{desc}} + x^{\mathrm{trans}} with x^{\mathrm{desc}}\in Z(A) and x^{\mathrm{trans}}\in[A,A], and this is the only such decomposition of x.
  2. \pi_Z is idempotent and Z(A)-linear: \pi_Z(zx) = z\,\pi_Z(x) for z\in Z(A).
  3. (Traces.) For every K-linear \tau : A\to M with \tau(ab)=\tau(ba): \tau(x)=\tau(x^{\mathrm{desc}}) and \tau(x^{\mathrm{trans}})=0.
  4. (Symmetries.) \pi_Z\circ\theta = \theta\circ\pi_Z for every K-algebra automorphism \theta and for every K-linear anti-automorphism \theta.
  5. \theta_Z is an involution. It is the identity on Z(A) and -\mathrm{id} on [A,A].
  6. (Classical; cited, not proved here.) If K is a field and A\cong\bigoplus_\lambda M_{d_\lambda}(K) is split semisimple with every d_\lambda invertible in K, then A has a centre–cocentre splitting and \pi_Z(x) = \sum_\lambda \frac{\chi^\lambda(x)}{d_\lambda}\,e_\lambda, where \chi^\lambda is the block trace and e_\lambda the central idempotent of the block. This applies to H_n(q) over \mathbb{Q}(q). For the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M=\sum_\lambda y_\lambda\chi^\lambda it gives \mathrm{tr}_M(x)=\mathrm{tr}_M(\pi_Z x).
  7. (The descent idempotent is not this projection.) Let n\ge2, let \ell : H_n(q)\hookrightarrow H_{n+1}(q) be the standard inclusion and \mathfrak d any K-linear left inverse of it (\mathfrak d \circ \ell = \mathrm{id}_{H_n(q)}). Then the image of \hat\tau_n = \ell\circ\mathfrak d of Descent involution is not contained in Z(H_{n+1}(q)). (The proof exhibits g_1 in the image and checks non-centrality in an explicit matrix representation of H_3(q); that the matrices satisfy the Hecke presentation is verified by hand.)

Item 3 refines Hochschild homology: every trace factors through HH_0 = A/[A,A], and under the splitting Z(A)\to A/[A,A] is an isomorphism. Item 7 says that the descended part of the corpus's descent idempotent is not central in general.
prf:centre-cocentre-descent:
Proof Proof of the centre–cocentre splitting. Items 1–2. Existence is the direct-sum decomposition. For uniqueness, apply \pi_Z to x = z + c with z\in Z(A), c\in[A,A]: since \pi_Z(z)=z and \pi_Z(c)=0, \pi_Z(x)=z and then c = x-z. Idempotence holds because \pi_Z(x)\in Z(A) is fixed by \pi_Z. For z\in Z(A), zx = z\,x^{\mathrm{desc}} + z\,x^{\mathrm{trans}}; the first term is central, and z[a,b]=[za,b], so z[A,A]\subseteq[A,A]. Uniqueness gives \pi_Z(zx)=z\,\pi_Z(x).

Item 3. A trace vanishes on each ab-ba, hence on their span [A,A]; apply it to x^{\mathrm{trans}}.

Item 4. An automorphism or anti-automorphism \theta maps Z(A) onto Z(A). It maps commutators to commutators: \theta(ab-ba) = \theta a\,\theta b-\theta b\,\theta a, or its negative for an anti-automorphism. So \theta[A,A]\subseteq[A,A], and uniqueness applied to \theta x = \theta x^{\mathrm{desc}}+\theta x^{\mathrm{trans}} gives \pi_Z(\theta x)=\theta(\pi_Z x).

Item 5. \pi_Z(\theta_Z x) = 2\pi_Z x-\pi_Z x = \pi_Z x, so \theta_Z(\theta_Z x) = 2\pi_Z x-(2\pi_Z x - x) = x. On Z(A), \theta_Z=\mathrm{id}; on [A,A], \theta_Z=-\mathrm{id}.

Item 6. It suffices to treat one block M_d(K) with d\in K^\times. Its centre is K\cdot1. Its commutator span is \mathfrak{sl}_d: commutators are traceless, and E_{ij}=[E_{ii},E_{ij}] for i\ne j and E_{ii}-E_{jj}=[E_{ij},E_{ji}] span \mathfrak{sl}_d. The intersection is 0 because c\cdot 1 traceless means cd=0. The sum is everything: x = \frac{\mathrm{tr}\,x}{d}\cdot 1+(x-\frac{\mathrm{tr}\,x}{d}\cdot1). Summing over blocks gives the formula. For H_n(q) over \mathbb{Q}(q) the Wedderburn decomposition is [Dipper–James 1986] and [Geck–Pfeiffer 2000, Ch. 8–9], with d_\lambda the number of standard tableaux, a positive integer. The Markov-trace line is item 3.

Item 7. Since \mathfrak d\circ\ell=\mathrm{id}, \hat\tau_n\circ\ell=\ell, so g_1=\ell(g_1) lies in the image. Over any nontrivial commutative ring with q invertible, the matrices

G_1=\begin{pmatrix}q&1\\0&-q^{-1}\end{pmatrix},\qquad G_2=\begin{pmatrix}-q^{-1}&0\\1&q\end{pmatrix}

satisfy G_i^2=(q-q^{-1})G_i+1 and G_1G_2G_1=G_2G_1G_2, so they define a representation of H_3(q). The (1,1) entry of G_1G_2-G_2G_1 is 1. So g_1g_2\ne g_2g_1 in H_3(q)\subseteq H_{n+1}(q), and g_1 is not central.

Items 1–5 hold over a generic commutative ring, and item 7 uses the standard presentation of H_3(q). The splitting hypothesis is not vacuous: it holds, for instance, for every commutative algebra. \blacksquare
conj:mass-categorical-descent:
Conjecture QOU mass formula as descent decomposition of the mass endomorphism. There is a mass element \mathfrak M(Z,N)\in H_n(q) and a functional \Phi with B(Z,N)=\Phi(\mathfrak M(Z,N)) such that, with \pi_Z the central projection of Centre–cocentre splitting:

  1. the volume, pairing and Wigner contributions to B(Z,N) depend only on the central part \pi_Z\mathfrak M, that is, on the central-character data \chi^\lambda(\mathfrak M)/d_\lambda;
  2. the surface, Coulomb, exchange-parity and shell contributions vanish when \mathfrak M is replaced by \pi_Z\mathfrak M.

What is proved is the algebra: Centre–cocentre splitting gives a unique split of an element into a central part and a commutator part whenever A=Z(A)\oplus[A,A], which holds for split semisimple H_n(q). Three consequences constrain this conjecture.

  • The split is of an element of the algebra, not of the number B(Z,N). A sum of \ln|\cdot| terms is not a linear functional of an element, so writing B=B^{\mathrm{desc}}+B^{\mathrm{trans}} has content only once \mathfrak M and \Phi are defined. Neither is defined in the corpus.
  • Every trace kills the commutator part (item 3 of the theorem). So if \Phi were a trace, the contributions in item 2 would be zero. A nonzero surface, Coulomb or shell sector needs a non-linear \Phi, such as the \ln|\cdot| form of Three-invariant atomic mass formula.
  • The descent idempotent \hat\tau_n=\ell_n\circ\mathfrak{d}_{n+1} of Descent involution is not the central projection: its image contains g_1, which is not central in H_{n+1}(q) for n\ge2 (item 7 of the theorem). In particular, the image of \hat\tau_n is not contained in the centre Z(H_{n+1}(q)).

Comparison (empirical; not part of any proved statement). Items 1 and 2 pair central-character data with the volume, pairing and Wigner terms of the liquid-drop model, and the rest with the surface, Coulomb, exchange-parity and magic-number shell terms. These are comparisons with the semi-empirical mass formula, whose Wigner term is itself a fitted empirical term, so the pairing cannot be used as a derivation of it. The further readings of the commutator part as localised on exceptional divisors of a brane blow-up, evaluated by quantum dilogarithm corrections, and as structuring the electromagnetic coupling, have no algebraic definition here and are not claimed.
rem:mass-categorical-descent-argument:
Remark Argument for mass categorical descent (not a proof). Argument (not a proof). Over a field R for which H_n(R,q) is split semisimple (e.g. q not a root of unity in characteristic 0), the Wedderburn–Artin decomposition H_n(R,q)\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda\vdash n}M_{d_\lambda}(R) identifies Z(H_n(q)) with the block scalars. Over a general commutative ring this decomposition does not hold. In the split semisimple case the algebra has a centre–cocentre splitting, and the central part of an element x is \sum_\lambda\frac{\chi^\lambda(x)}{d_\lambda}e_\lambda (Centre–cocentre splitting, item 6).

The scalar sum \mathfrak m=\sum_i\ln|M_i| is a real number rather than an element of H_n(q), so the algebra-level centre–cocentre split cannot be applied directly to \mathfrak m; labelling terms that factor through a block's Casimir eigenvalue as "descended" is a definition rather than a theorem. Consequently, the Wedderburn–Artin splitting establishes nothing beyond the theorem cited and does not derive the liquid-drop term pairings in the conjecture statement.
rem:wedderburn-trace-identity-context:
Remark Descent-decomposition role, scale-versus-weight distinction, and classical limit of the Wedderburn trace identity. The Wedderburn trace identity records the normalization of the Markov trace on the Wedderburn blocks of the Hecke algebra H_n(R, q): the total Markov weight is partitioned among the irreducible representations with unit sum, providing the combinatorial foundation for the descent decomposition of mass and coupling.

Consequence for mass.

In the descent decomposition of the mass endomorphism (BW as descent), the Markov weight y_\lambda of each partition \lambda fixes that block's contribution to the total binding energy; the unit-sum normalization is what makes the descent a genuine partition of the weight. The standard representation [n{-}1, 1] carries the dominant weight, which is why the volume term (sourced by the standard block) leads the BW formula.

Scale versus weight — two distinct q-objects.

Two q-quantities enter the BW formula and must not be conflated:

  • the Hecke-level scale [n]_q! = [1]_q [2]_q \cdots [n]_q — for example the Wigner coefficient \lambda_W = [5]_q!\, m_e at Hecke level k = 5 — evaluated directly as the q-factorial product;
  • the per-block weight ratio w_\lambda(q) = \dim_q(\lambda)^2 / [n]_q!, used in the LP-dual shadow prices, which coincides with the Markov weight y_\lambda only on self-conjugate \lambda.

Neither is the bare sum \sum_\lambda \dim_q(\lambda)^2: that sum is a separate q-polynomial — the global dimension of the block algebra — and equals [n]_q! only at q = 1.

Classical limit. At q = 1 the block dimensions satisfy the Wedderburn–Artin count \sum_\lambda d_\lambda^2 = n! = \dim H_n for \mathbb{C}[S_n]. Dividing by n! gives the unit-sum normalization for the Plancherel weights d_\lambda/n!, which are the Markov weights at z = 0 (the regular trace). At z = q^3/(q^2+1), setting q = 1 gives z = 1/2 and different weights: at n = 2, y_{(2)} = 3/4 and y_{(1,1)} = 1/4.
prop:descended-level-zero:
Proposition Descended mass contribution lives at level 0 only. For every jet level n \ge 0, the descended component of the mass integrand equals the invariant base-level holonomy:

  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}\!\bigl(\hat\tau_n(\alpha^{(n+1)})\bigr) \bigr\rVert
  \;=\;
  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho_0).

The descended term enters the tower sum exclusively at level 0. All higher levels contribute strictly transient divisor modes.

The descent involution is idempotent and factors recursively through lower levels. Iterating the trace reduction consistently recovers the base-level cycle mass. Summing the descended component at each subsequent jet level would double-count the base-level holonomy.
prop:jet-tower-convergence:
Proposition Geometric-series tail bound for the \hbar_q^2 brane-tower sum. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with substrate parameter q and Planck-q constant \hbar_q = (q-1)/q. For a vortex \varrho with braid representative \beta \in B_n, the brane-tower refinement of the mass endomorphism (mass tower, jet-brane reformulation) takes the form

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  = \mathfrak{m}^{(0)}(\varrho)
  + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \hbar_q^{2n} \cdot \Delta^{(n)}(\varrho),

where \mathfrak{m}^{(0)} is the canonical Markov-trace term at brane level zero and \Delta^{(n)}(\varrho) = \mathfrak{m}^{(n)} (\varrho_\mathrm{free}) - \mathfrak{m}^{(n)}(\varrho_\mathrm{atom}) is the per-level binding contribution at brane level n. The \hbar_q^{2n} weight comes from the recursive brane tower A_{n+1} = A_n \otimes \Omega^1(A_n): each jet-up step pairs a Kähler form with its Frobenius dual, contributing \hbar_q^2 to the weight.

Assume q > 1/2 and q \neq 1, so that 0 < \hbar_q^2 < 1, and assume there exists \Delta_{\max}(\varrho) < \infty with |\Delta^{(n)}(\varrho)| \leq \Delta_{\max}(\varrho) for all n \geq 1. Then the brane-tower sum T(\varrho) := \sum_{n \geq 1} \hbar_q^{2n} \Delta^{(n)}(\varrho) converges absolutely, and the N-term truncation error is bounded by

  \bigl\lvert T(\varrho)
    - \sum_{n=1}^{N} \hbar_q^{2n}\,\Delta^{(n)}(\varrho) \bigr\rvert
  \;\leq\; \Delta_{\max}(\varrho) \cdot
  \frac{\hbar_q^{2(N+1)}}{1 - \hbar_q^{2}}.

In particular, to achieve binding-energy precision \varepsilon_B (in MeV) at archimedean calibration E_0, it suffices to take

  N \;\geq\;
  \left\lceil \frac{\log\bigl( \tfrac{\varepsilon_B \,(1 - \hbar_q^{2})}
                                {E_0 \,\Delta_{\max}(\varrho)} \bigr)}
                 {\log(\hbar_q^{2})} \right\rceil.

The discussion of the boundedness hypothesis, the engineering consequence, and the relation to the confinement SDP are collected in the jet-tower convergence context.
prf:jet-tower-convergence:
Proof Proof of jet tower convergence. The geometric series \sum_{k \geq 0} \hbar_q^{2k} converges with sum (1 - \hbar_q^{2})^{-1} because \hbar_q^2 \in (0, 1) for q > 1/2, q \neq 1 (indeed \hbar_q^2 \approx 0.00982 at q_0 \approx 1.11). Absolute convergence follows from the comparison \sum_{n \geq 1} \hbar_q^{2n} |\Delta^{(n)}| \leq \Delta_{\max} \sum_{n \geq 1} \hbar_q^{2n} = \Delta_{\max} \cdot \hbar_q^2 / (1 - \hbar_q^2). The tail bound factors the first skipped term:

  \bigl\lvert \sum_{n > N} \hbar_q^{2n}\,\Delta^{(n)} \bigr\rvert
  \leq \Delta_{\max} \cdot \hbar_q^{2(N+1)}
   \sum_{k \geq 0} \hbar_q^{2k}
  = \Delta_{\max} \cdot \frac{\hbar_q^{2(N+1)}}{1 - \hbar_q^{2}}.

Multiplying by E_0 and solving E_0 \cdot \Delta_{\max} \cdot \hbar_q^{2(N+1)} / (1 - \hbar_q^2) \leq \varepsilon_B for N gives the stated count. \square
lem:vhat-pair-commutation-trace:
Lemma Pair commutation at the traced-volume level: \hat V_i \hat V_j = \hat V_j \hat V_i in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, z]. Let \hat V_i(q) = z(q)a_i(q) + b_i(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, z] be the traced volume of the i-th crossing of a closed braid. For any two indices i, j:

  \hat V_i(q) \cdot \hat V_j(q)
  \;=\;
  \hat V_j(q) \cdot \hat V_i(q)
  \qquad
  \text{in } \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, z].

Equivalently:

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\hat V_i \hat V_j\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\hat V_j \hat V_i\bigr)
  \;=\; z^2.

The pentagon identity requirement uv = qvu applies strictly to non-commutative operator lifts, not to the scalar traced volumes. The traced volumes commute exactly.
prop:markov-pair-z2:
Proposition All-pairs Markov-trace identity \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i\sigma_j) = z^2. Let H_n(R, q) be the Iwahori--Hecke algebra with Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M normalised by \mathrm{tr}_M(1_k) = 1 for all k and Markov axiom \mathrm{tr}_M(x\sigma_{k-1}) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) for x \in H_{k-1}(q), where z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) (Jones--Markov trace).

For every pair of braid generators \sigma_i, \sigma_j with 0 \le i < j, embedded in any H_n(R, q) with n > j,

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i\sigma_j) \;=\; z^2.

The identity holds whether (i,j) are adjacent (j = i+1) or non-adjacent (j \ge i+2).
prf:markov-pair-z2:
Proof Proof of markov pair z2. The argument is a direct two-step peel, one Markov move per factor. Embed \sigma_i\sigma_j in H_{j+1}(q), the minimal Hecke algebra containing both generators; higher embeddings follow by Markov closure \mathrm{tr}_M^{H_n} = \mathrm{tr}_M^{H_{n-1}} on any element of H_{n-1}(q) embedded in H_n(R, q).

Peel 1 (outer generator). In H_{j+1}(q) the rightmost generator is \sigma_j. Since \sigma_i \in H_j(q) (it involves only indices \le j-1), \sigma_i commutes by definition with the coefficient ring and is not affected by the Markov move on \sigma_j:

  \mathrm{tr}_M^{H_{j+1}}\!(\sigma_i\sigma_j)
  \;=\; z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M^{H_j}\!(\sigma_i).

Peel 2 (inner generator). The remaining element \sigma_i lives in H_j(q). Repeatedly apply Markov closure to reduce to the minimal embedding \sigma_i \in H_{i+2}(q):

  \mathrm{tr}_M^{H_j}\!(\sigma_i)
  \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M^{H_{j-1}}\!(\sigma_i)
  \;=\; \cdots \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{H_{i+2}}\!(\sigma_i).

In H_{i+2}(q), \sigma_i itself is the rightmost generator. Apply the Markov axiom once more:

  \mathrm{tr}_M^{H_{i+2}}\!(\sigma_i)
  \;=\; z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M^{H_{i+1}}\!(1)
  \;=\; z.

Combining the two peels: \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i\sigma_j) = z \cdot z = z^2. \square
prf:vhat-pair-commutation-trace:
Proof Proof of vhat pair commutation trace. The traced volume \hat V_i(q) = z(q)\,a_i(q) + b_i(q) is, by construction (def:algebraic-quantum-volume §partial-product expansion), an element of the commutative Laurent polynomial ring \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, z] — the coefficients a_i, b_i are polynomials in q^{\pm 1/2} and z is a single transcendental parameter (the Markov parameter, eliminated by z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) at the end of every Markov peel, Existence and non-degeneracy of the Markov trace (Jones, 1987)).

Two elements of a commutative ring commute. Hence

  \hat V_i \cdot \hat V_j \;=\; \hat V_j \cdot \hat V_i.

Applying \mathrm{tr}_M (which is \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, z]- linear) and invoking the pair Markov-trace identity (prop:markov-pair-z2) gives the second equality \mathrm{tr}_M(\hat V_i \hat V_j) = z^2 for all i, j — adjacent or not. \square
prop:pentagon-uv-commutation:
Proposition Pentagon identity at adjacent jet levels: \widehat U \widehat V = q\,\widehat V \widehat U. The pentagon identity of the quantum dilogarithm (quantum Bloch group)

  \Phi_q(v)\,\Phi_q(u) \;=\; \Phi_q(u)\,\Phi_q(uv)\,\Phi_q(v)

requires the quantum-torus relation uv = q\,vu on its operator arguments. This remark places that relation in the brane-tower formalism and how it drives the jet-tower mass ascension.
prop:delta-max-uniform-bound:
Proposition Uniform bound on the per-level jet residual |\Delta^{(n)}|. Let \varrho have braid representative \beta \in B_n with Hecke image \rho(\beta) \in H_n(R, q) in the standard representation. Let

  \|\rho(\beta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
  \;=\;
  \sup_{\|\psi\|=1} \|\rho(\beta)\psi\|

be the operator norm on the Jones--Wenzl module, and let L(\beta) denote the braid length (number of generator factors). Then for all n \ge 1,

  |\Delta^{(n)}(\varrho)|
  \;\leq\;
  \Delta_{\max}(\varrho)
  \;:=\;
  2\,L(\beta)\,\|\rho(\beta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{2}\,
  \cdot\, \mathfrak{m}^{(0)}(\varrho_{\mathrm{free}}),

independent of the jet level n.
rem:delta-max-uniform-bound-context:
Remark Framework context for the uniform tail bound. This proposition is tightly coupled to the \Phi_q-tower binding pipeline. The active framework instead uses JSJ decomposition with hyperbolic volumes; the result here is retained as the analogous tail bound on the \Phi_q side and remains mathematically correct.

The jet-tower tail bound (jet-tower convergence) is conditional on a uniform bound |\Delta^{(n)}(\varrho)| \leq \Delta_{\max}(\varrho) across jet levels n \ge 1. This proposition supplies an explicit \Delta_{\max} from operator-norm estimates on the Hecke standard representation, closing the open hypothesis in the archimedean (SDP rank-1) regime.
rem:mass-tower-syt-cells: Remark SYT / Jucys–Murphy reindexing of the mass tower pair set. This remark reframes the pair blow-up set \mathcal{P}_n (jet-brane reformulation) using the Jucys--Murphy (JM) elements and standard Young tableaux (SYT). The motivation: empirical probes show the optimal \mathcal{P}_n is all pairs with no distance restriction ([descent rate categorical](#sim:descent-rate-canonical evaluation)), which is most accordingly expressed in the JM / SYT cell basis.
prose:intro-mutant-jones-bloch-group:
A classic limitation of the uncolored Jones polynomial—and hence of the bare closure Markov trace—is its inability to distinguish mutant knots such as the 11-crossing Conway and Kinoshita–Terasaka pair, which differ by a 180^\circ Conway-sphere involution yet have distinct hyperbolic volumes (\mathrm{Vol}(\mathrm{KT}) \neq \mathrm{Vol}(\mathrm{Conway})).

This section shows how the bi-filtered Hecke framework resolves mutant ambiguity. Whereas the level-zero closure trace collapses the four-strand Conway tangle to a symmetric scalar, the knot-indexed convolution grid and the non-commutative Wedderburn Fourier transform retain the off-diagonal representation matrix elements before closure. Pushing these representation invariants into the Bloch group B(\mathbb{C}) separates the Conway and Kinoshita–Terasaka complements, links the Pieri photon shift and JSJ tower bridge to the WKB Green's function of the quantum dilogarithm, and identifies the Borromean complement's class in the Bloch group via Poincaré–Lefschetz duality.

Proposition Placement of paper's existing knot-indexed convolutions in the bi-filtration grid. Each operational non-tensor product linking two morphisms in the QOU occupies a specific (n, K) stratum in the bi-filtration grid \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)}.

The grid structure and its role in separating input shape from output transcendence depth are described in the convolution-grid context.

conj:categorical-higgs-mechanism:
Conjecture Categorical Higgs mechanism: Goldstone-eating as topological linking. The symmetry-breaking Higgs mechanism SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y \to U(1)_{\rm em} admits a categorical formulation. Goldstone boson consumption corresponds exactly to the topological linking of closed braids.

Pre-symmetry breaking, the four electroweak gauge bosons form individual 1-component knots. A Higgs doublet provides four real scalar degrees of freedom, also corresponding to 1-component knots.

Post-breaking, the vacuum expectation value induces topological linking. Three gauge bosons each fuse with a Goldstone boson, forming 2-component links. The linking number \mathrm{lk} = 1 encodes the broken-generator multiplicity. The remaining unbroken photon survives as a 1-component knot. The surviving Higgs scalar similarly remains an independent mediator.

The mass of each post-breaking boson evaluates as the Markov trace of its new 2-component link, weighted by the appropriate Hoefsmit projector. Categorical linking supplies the precise operation that differentiates massive force-links from massless matter-knots.
conj:categorical-linking-operation:
Conjecture Categorical linking operation \mathrm{Lk}_R: ribbon-category dual of topological linking number. Let \mathbf{C} be a rigid monoidal R-linear category with braiding c_{X, Y}, and let A be the Frobenius-Hopf substrate. The categorical linking operation is the family of R-linear maps

  \mathrm{Lk}_R^{(k)}
  \;\colon\;
  \mathrm{Hom}_R(\mathbf{1}, A) \otimes_R \mathrm{Hom}_R(\mathbf{1}, A)
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \mathrm{End}_R(A),

defined by

  \mathrm{Lk}_R^{(k)}(a, b)
  \;:=\;
  (\mathrm{id}_A \otimes \tau_R) \,\circ\,
  \bigl( c_{A, A}^{\,k} \circ (a \otimes b) \otimes \mathrm{id}_A \bigr)
  \,\circ\, \mathrm{id}_A.

This evaluates the categorical trace-cut of a 2-component link: closing one component via the trace leaves the other as a free endomorphism.
rem:categorical-linking-operation-interp: Remark Proof scope of Property 1: linearity is a generic categorical fact. The proofs for properties 1-3 utilize only standard rigid monoidal axioms. They apply generically across any suitable category supporting trace-cuts and require no QOU-specific Hecke algebra or Markov trace assumptions.

rem:conway-kt-vol-injectivity-test:
Remark Conway--Kinoshita--Terasaka mutant pair: a volume-injectivity check for the depth correspondence. The transcendental accounting framework predicts that identical Jones polynomials imply identical hyperbolic volumes. The Conway and Kinoshita-Terasaka mutant knots share exactly the same Jones polynomial and the same hyperbolic volume, satisfying this prediction.

Mutation preserves the colored Jones polynomials and the hyperbolic volume universally (Ruberman's theorem). The prediction therefore holds trivially for mutants.

For rigorous falsifiability, the Vol-injectivity hypothesis requires a non-mutant knot pair sharing identical Jones polynomials but exhibiting distinct hyperbolic volumes. No such pairs are currently known within the Bring-embeddable class. Discovering one would strictly falsify the J^{(2)} Vol-injectivity claim, though the higher-color asymptotic Volume Conjecture mechanism would remain mathematically consistent.
rem:jones-faithfulness-crossing-8:
Remark Bring-embeddable Jones-faithfulness: theorem at crossing \leq 10, falsified for Conway-KT at crossing 11. The Hoste-Thistlethwaite-Weeks enumeration proved that distinct prime knots up to 10 crossings possess unique Jones polynomials. The Conway-KT mutant pair breaks this uniqueness precisely at 11 crossings.

Since both the Conway and KT knots are Bring-embeddable (genus 3), Jones-faithfulness strictly fails for Bring-embeddable knots at crossing 11. However, Ruberman's theorem forces their volumes to match, maintaining the Vol-injectivity prediction. The open challenge remains locating non-mutant Jones-coincident pairs above 11 crossings to construct a definitive falsification target.
prop:wedderburn-as-noncomm-fourier:
Proposition The Wedderburn--Artin mass sum is the inverse non-commutative Fourier transform on H_n(q). Statement. The character expansion driving the three-invariant mass formula operates identically to the inverse non-commutative Fourier transform on the semisimple Hecke algebra H_n(q).

The mechanism and its role in the mass formula are described in the non-commutative-Fourier reading.
rem:wedderburn-as-noncomm-fourier-contex:
Remark The mass formula as an inverse non-commutative Fourier transform. The Wedderburn-Artin decomposition maps the Markov trace into a spectral expansion over partitions. The trace reassembles class functions directly from these non-commutative Fourier coefficients.

The identification introduces no new physics. The mechanism is that the mass formula evaluates specific physical channels by selecting isolated partitions from the non-commutative spectrum. The identification governs the Pieri-shift dynamics of the Hecke photon and the spectral distribution of the archimedean remainder.
lem:degree-one-braid-trivial-volume:
Lemma Braid words of a degree-one element have non-hyperbolic closures. Statement. Let \gamma = c_0\,\mathbf{1} + \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} \phi_i\, \sigma_i^{\epsilon_i}, with \epsilon_i \in \{\pm 1\}, be a degree-one element of H_n(q). Every braid word in the support of \gamma has a non-hyperbolic closure: \overline{\mathbf{1}} is the n-component unlink and \overline{\sigma_i^{\pm 1}} is the (n-1)-component unlink. Hence the hyperbolic volume vanishes word by word:

  \mathrm{Vol}\bigl(\overline{w}\bigr) \;=\; 0
  \qquad \text{for every word } w \in \{\mathbf{1}, \sigma_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, \sigma_{n-1}^{\pm 1}\}.

The volume is a function on braid words, not a linear map on H_n(q). No linear map on H_n(q) agrees with the hyperbolic volume on all braid words, so the statement does not extend to a volume of the element \gamma itself.

The same holds for a photon \gamma(\varphi) = \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\,\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} \in H_3(q). Its support words are \mathbf{1}, \sigma_0, \sigma_1, \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}. They close to the three-component unlink, the two-component unlink (twice) and the unknot. The vertex word \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} uses each generator once, so its closure is the unknot. Every support word of a photon therefore has volume 0. The degree-one element above is not a photon, because it has no vertex term. On one strand pair with all \epsilon_i = +1 and c_0 = 1 it is the photon's specialisation \varphi_{01} = 0.
prop:pieri-photon-shift:
Proposition Multiplication by a degree-one Hecke element is a non-commutative Fourier shift (Pieri rule). Statement. Let \lambda = (\lambda_1, \lambda_2) \vdash n be a partition with at most two rows (the shapes seen by \mathrm{SU}_q(2) on V_\square^{\otimes n}), and let \beta_m \in H_n(q) be supported purely on the \lambda-block. Let \gamma be a photon \gamma(\varphi) = \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\sigma_a + \varphi_1\sigma_b + \varphi_{01}\,\sigma_a\sigma_b^{-1} on consecutive generators a, b = a + 1 with b \leq n, so that at most one of its three strands lies beyond the n strands of \beta_m (its degree-one specialisation \varphi_{01} = 0 included).

  1. If b \leq n - 1, then \gamma\beta_m \in H_n(q) and \mathrm{supp}(\gamma\beta_m) \subseteq \{\lambda\}.
  2. If b = n, read \gamma\beta_m in H_{n+1}(q). Its Wedderburn support is contained in the set of \mu \vdash n + 1 with \mu \supset \lambda, namely \lambda + \square := (\lambda_1 + 1, \lambda_2), \lambda - \square := (\lambda_1, \lambda_2 + 1) (when it is a partition) and (\lambda_1, \lambda_2, 1). On V_\square^{\otimes(n+1)} the three-row component acts by zero, so there
  \mathrm{supp}\bigl(\gamma \cdot \beta_m\bigr)
  \;\subseteq\;
  \{\lambda + \square\} \;\cup\; \{\lambda - \square\}.

The name \lambda - \square comes from the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) reading: a complete two-box column is the trivial weight, so (\lambda_1, \lambda_2 + 1) has the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) highest weight of (\lambda_1 - 1, \lambda_2). As a partition it has one box more than \lambda, not one less.

The case a = n (two strands beyond \beta_m) is not covered: there the product lies in H_{n+2}(q) and the support can reach partitions with two more boxes.
